key_insight: Classical texture and gradient features can separate COVID-19 from other pneumonia better than chance, but only modestly in this small pilot study.
clinical_relevance: This work suggests chest X-ray-based AI may help with pulmonary disease triage, though the reported performance is not yet strong enough for clinical use.
method: Used public chest X-ray data from 408 patients (668 radiographs).
Extracted HOG and GLCM texture features.
Trained logistic regression, random forest, and SVM models with patient-level 5-fold stratified cross-validation.
evidence_signal: Best performance was 75.4% mean accuracy with AUC 0.755, compared with a 71.6% majority-class baseline, using patient-level cross-validation to reduce leakage.
watch_item: The dataset is small and limited to one public source, so broader validation on multi-institutional, ethically sourced data is still needed.
paper_title: Toward Multi-Modal Deep Learning for Pulmonary Disease Classification: A Texture-Based Machine Learning Pilot Study on Public Chest X-Ray Data
